articleTitle: Approximate Three-Operand Binary Adder for Error-Resilient Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper presents an approximate three-operand adder, highlighting its advantages in terms of speed, power consumption, and area utilization compared to conventional adders. an approximate three-operand adder is designed using 45 nm technology. The adders are implemented for 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit operands. A comprehensive comparison of these adders in terms of area, power, and delay is presented. Accuracy metrics, including error distance, error rate, MED, and NED are also computed to evaluate the performance of the proposed adder. The results show that the proposed approximate adder is 1.1 times faster than the existing adder, consumes 18% less power, and utilizes 12% less core area. These improvements make it an attractive choice for practical applications. To further demonstrate its efficiency, an image-processing application is included in the paper. The evaluation metrics confirm the effectiveness of the proposed design, making it a promising option for various error-resilient applications like multimedia and image-processing.

articleTitle: Lite-Agro 2.0: Integrating Federated and TinyML in Pear Disease Classification IoAT-Edge AI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The success of Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) is dependent on the process of the model training, along with optimized algorithms and quality image dataset. In the process of Pear disease identification through tree leaf analysis, the need to protect the privacy of protected data has led to the topic of Federated Learning (FL). Prior Lite-Agro 1.0 study aims to apply Neural Network trained Deep Learning models on lightweight MCUs. With this second Lite-Agro 2.0 expansion, we explore different models, the integration of Federated Averaging (FedAvg) algorithm and explore decentralized training of models on multiple client devices with an emphasis on preserving data privacy. In federated learning, the data does not leave the client device and individual weights are passed on and aggregated onto a global server which then generates a global model. This federated learning research benchmarks frameworks such as Flower. Dev, model performance, and tabulates training values such as accuracy and loss given various FedAvg algorithms.

articleTitle: Security Evaluation of Lightweight SBoxes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive evaluation of the security properties of lightweight substitution boxes (SBoxes), which are essential components of cryptographic algorithms designed for resource-constrained devices. The evaluation encompasses various aspects, such as the non-linearity of the SBoxes, algebraic degree, etc., to assess their vulnerability to linear and differential cryptanalysis. These insights enable informed decision-making when selecting SBox designs that meet specific cryptographic requirements. The analysis of existing lightweight SBox designs serves as a foundation for future research and development in the field of lightweight cryptography, contributing to advancements in the field, and promoting the secure implementation of cryptographic systems in real-world applications.

articleTitle: A Fall Detection System using Hybrid Inertial and Physiological Signal Classifiers for Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: In this modern day and age, passive health monitoring and event alert systems are crucial in redefining healthcare for future generations. Among other health events, Accidental Fall is one of the leading causes of injuries in the elderly, who make up about three-quarters of the total victim pool. This study focuses on low latency, power-efficient implementation of an accidental Fall Detection system in dynamic environments (indoor and outdoor) from Accelerometer and PPG sensor data, using a hybrid CNN-kNN estimator for computation at the edge. Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs), the foundation for almost all image processing and classification models, are used here to independently estimate the representative probability of motion in individual axes. The k-Nearest Neighbour (kNN) algorithm classifies if the event is a fall considering the features from the CNN inter-dependently, correlating them as it would in case of an accidental fall, with a shallow computational requirement. Our proposed design thus focuses on an efficient and custom Independent Axis Inertial Analysis (2IA) design for motion and vital signal analysis, along with a Dependent Analysis (DA) model for the final fall estimation.

articleTitle: Assist Techniques for Radiation Hardened SRAM in Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Space offers harsh environment such as high energy particles and high temperature fluctuations. This harsh environment causes single event upsets (SEUs). Conventional6T SRAM is unable to withstand this harsh environment and it also has very low critical charge (Qc). Hence it is necessary to use radiation hardened SRAM which will be resistant to SEUs and will be able to recover from SEUs/soft errors on its own. Researchers over the years have proposed many radiation hardened SRAM cells. Out of these the four recently proposed radiation hardened cells are RHBD IoT, RHMD IoT, SRRD 12T and RHPD 12T. The design metrics of each of these bitcells have been evaluated and their Electric Quality metric (EQM) which judges the overall performance of the bitcell has been estimated. Finally, read/write assist techniques have been applied to each of these bitcells to improve the read/write design metrics and hence improve the overall EQM value.

articleTitle: Approximate CNN on FPGA Using Toom-Cook Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Deep Learning algorithms are widely used in most of the computer vision applications in real-world scenario. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a promising deep learning technique, which provides high accuracy for classification tasks. On the other hand, it requires significant computational resources, when compared with conventional algorithms. Latest CNNs have millions of parameters and are not advantageous for edge devices with memory and power constraints. Techniques like approximation aims to minimize the number of computations needed for inference. Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FP-GAs) are suitable hardware solutions for edge computing, when compared to software solutions like General Purpose Processors and GPUs (Graphic Processing Units). FPGA gives better power consumption and is a flexible hardware. In this paper we propose an approximate CNN architecture which uses Toom-Cook based approximate multiplier for efficient inference. The proposed approximate CNN architecture has been implemented on Virtex UltraScale+ FPGA with an operating frequency of 150 MHz and achieved comparable performance with existing implementations. An accuracy of 96% has been reported by the proposed architecture.

articleTitle: A 0.5V Energy Efficient All CMOS Temperature Sensor for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This article proposes an energy efficient low-power temperature sensor based on CMOS technology for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. The sensor operation relies on temperature-independent/dependent current sources followed by the current controlled oscillators (CCO) that generate a frequency that varies with the temperature. A Frequency-to-digital converter (FDC) is employed to convert the frequency into digital value. Moreover, the temperature sensor is operated in a sub-threshold region and an external clock reference signal is used to minimize power consumption. The proposed temperature sensor has a power consumption of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.33 \mu \mathrm{w}$</tex> with a resolution of 0.1 o C while operating with a power supply of 0.5V. The sensor is simulated in a standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18 \mu m$</tex> CMOS technology with an active area of 0.0205 mm ‘. Furthermore, the experimental results illustrate that the proposed work attains an accuracy of −1 /+0.91 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ \mathrm{C}$</tex> across <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$125^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> temperature range and a Resolution FoM of 2.71 pJ.K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>•

articleTitle: Real Time Voice Recognition System using Tiny ML on Arduino Nano 33 BLE *
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This Paper outlines the creation, construction, and evaluation of a Real-Time Voice Recognition System using TinyML on an Arduino Nano 33 BLE, a hardware platform with limited resources. Tiny ML consists of machine learning models that can be deployed on the low -energy and resource- constrained embedded system. Real-time voice Recognition is used in virtual assistants like Siri, Google Assistant, Alexa, speech-to-text translation, vehicle Navigation, voice biometrics, home automation etc. The work presents the implementation of real-time voice recognition wherein a TinyML model is trained using the EdgeImpulse framework and deployed on Arduino Nano 33 BLE device having a built-in microphone. The model identifies the ON and STOP keywords pronounced by the user using Arduino Nano 33 BLE device's built-in microphone which then turns on a bulb connected to it via a relay. The accuracy of the system is found to be 97 %.

articleTitle: Automated Polynomial Formal Verification: Human-Readable Proof Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The importance of verification of digital circuits has increased significantly, as their complexity has grown. Simulation based techniques cannot fully guarantee their correctness, as the correctness has to be shown for every possible input assignment. Thus, formal verification has to be applied. However, formal verification methods may require exponential time and space in the worst case. Therefore, Polynomial Formal Verification (PFV) has been researched in the past years, where polynomial upper bounds have been proven for the complete formal verification process. By this efficient run times of the tools are guaranteed. Polynomial bounds have been proven successfully for the verification of several types of circuits, like e.g. adders and multipliers. However, due to the lack of automation techniques, all previous proofs were conducted manually. A tool enabling the automatic proof generation has recently been introduced, which demonstrates the concept of automatic proofs on the example of Binary Decision Diagrams (BDDs). We enhance the tool to automatically generate an extended human-readable proof, detailing the automatic reasoning, such that the produced proof is fully comprehensible.

articleTitle: Paninis's Grammar as Computer Language: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: An ancient and classical language from South Asia is Sanskrit. Today, it is spoken by about 25,000 people in India, but it has influenced many other languages and communities worldwide. It has contributed to some of India's oldest knowledge. This paper aims to study, understand and analyze the existing theories on Sanskrit grammar as a computer language and highlight how the Astadhyayi influences the compiler design. It also discusses the experiment done for Sanskrit-Hindi Machine Translation by embedding syntactic features. We achieve this by setting up the model on Sanskrit-English and English-Hindi language sets. We also include a more extensive set of syntactic features by generating syntactic trees and performing graph traversals to create sequential memory blocks. This methodology benefits the learning of Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models by lessening the data sparseness issue and helping resolve the long-distance reliance on words in the baseline NMT models. An experimental analysis is done, and the comparison of results shows improved interpretation quality.

articleTitle: A Memory Efficient Run-time Re-configurable Convolution IP Core for Deep Neural Networks Inference on FPGA Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Modern computer vision applications are vastly dependent on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in order to perform feature extractions, dimensionality reduction, etc. There are a series of arithmetic calculations markedly dominated by multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations in a single convolutional layer which is directly dependent on the kernel size. In this work, we propose a design method for a run-time re-configurable convolution IP core which could be implemented for any layer of a CNN having variable kernel sizes and verified for different dimensions, 5 × 5 for LeNet-5 and 11 × 11 for AlexNet respectively. The proposed accelerator is 6.25 x and 12.1 x faster than basic MAC operation for LeNet-5 and AlexNet respectively. The design has been compared with existing architecture and has improved performance by 2.46x G(FL)OPS/s per MAC module. Our proposed design has run-time re-configuration support with a scheduler logic which empowers to realize the design for any specific layer, kernel dimension and channels for respectively with efficient resource utilization.

articleTitle: Accelerating Sorting Performance on FPGA: Combining Quick Sort and Heap Sort through Hybrid Pipelining
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Hybrid pipelined sorting is a technique that com-bines the benefits of pipelined sorting and hybrid sorting algorithms. Top-k sorting is an algorithm that sorts only the top-k elements of a collection instead of sorting the entire collection. Top-k sorting is a variation of sorting where only the k largest (or smallest) elements in a dataset need to be sorted, rather than the entire dataset. This algorithm is often used when the collection is too large to be sorted entirely or when we only need the top <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> elements for some operation. However, the current FPGA-based implementation solutions face issues with sorting in high-performance scenarios. These problems are further compounded by the top-k sorting architecture. To address these issues, we propose a solution that improves throughput and decreases latency during the process. This is achieved by integrating quicksort and heap-based sorting algorithms, which overcome the limitations of the bitonic sort algorithm. The proposed architecture combines the strengths of both quicksort and heap-based sorting algorithms to achieve high performance while minimizing hardware resource utilization. The proposed sorting algorithm is synthesized and simulated using Vivado design suit 2022.2 and implemented on a Kintex-7 FPGA board.

articleTitle: Drone based Potholes detection using Machine Learning on various Edge AI devices in Real-Time
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Pothole detection is an important aspect of road maintenance and safety. The presence of potholes on roads can cause damage to vehicles, create safety hazards for drivers, and increase maintenance costs. Timely detection of potholes can alert the driver for better navigation as well as the location of the potholes can be shared with the local governing body for taking counteractions. In this paper, we have detected potholes using two object detection models, YOLOv5, YOLOv7 & YOLOv8 and have employed the trained models on Edge AI Devices for real-time inference. We have compared the outcomes of YOLO in terms of accuracy, precision and recall. YOLOv8 is giving 78% of accuracy, YOLOv7 is giving 67% of accuracy and YOLOv5 is giving 70% of accuracy. These models are deployed on Raspberry Pi-4, Nvidia Jetson Nano and Intel UP Squared board. The performance of these Edge AI devices is analyzed in terms of fps and through experimental results it is observed that the Intel UP Squared board achieves higher fps. For real-time detection of potholes, live videos were collected through drones and were live streamed to the Edge AI devices through the RTMP server for real-time inference. Overall, the proposed system is highly efficient for the reliable detection of potholes under different road conditions.

articleTitle: Design & Implementation of Novel Asynchronous FIFO
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Asynchronous First Input First Output (FIFO) is frequently utilized to address the issue of data transmission across the clock domain due to the rapid advancement of integrated circuits. The creation of empty-full signals, the primary challenge of asynchronous FIFO design, is primarily examined in this study. The paper's primary goal is to accomplish similar capabilities without the use of a synchronizer. However, by doing so, just a portion of the performance is lost, and the asynchronous FIFO continues to function as intended. The developed asynchronous FIFO can realize first-in, first-out of data and accurately create empty and full signals thanks to Xilinx Vivado 2023 simulation verification, which satisfies the design requirements. The study in this paper is beneficial for further asynchronous FIFO application in data transmission across. As per simulation reports power dissipation is increased by 6.9195 % & Utilization is decreased by 40.43% due to update in algorithmic level of abstraction in asynchronous FIFO.

articleTitle: Practical Analysis of Various Approaches for Targeting Delay Faults at Functional Frequency in Automatic Test Pattern Generation (ATPG)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Delay faults in VLSI testing are a crucial aspect in ensuring the quality of the final chip and for optimizing testing coverage and time. It is important to detect these faults to minimize errors and maximize efficiency. At-speed testing methodologies offer a promising approach to detecting delay faults, but these methods must be carefully optimized to achieve high coverage and test time efficiency. This research focuses on evaluating practical at-speed testing methodologies for delay fault detection. That at-speed testing techniques are comprehensively described, compared, and evaluated from practical implementation perspectives. Furthermore, this study highlights the significance of practical validation in assessing the performance of these methodologies. Experimental results, obtained using an automatic test pattern generation tool, are presented, and rigorous simulations are conducted to verify the correctness of the generated test patterns. By advancing at-speed testing methodologies and emphasizing practical validation, this study aims to compares and evaluates existing at-speed testing methodologies for delay fault detection, identifying the most suitable methods for different applications and enhancing their effectiveness. The outcomes underscore the importance of optimizing coverage and test time while ensuring accurate fault detection. The work is being carried out using peripheral router on the platform Synopsys TetraMAX, Synopsys DFT and Synopsys VCS

articleTitle: Acoustic Based Chicken Health Monitoring in Smart Poultry Farms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Poultry farming's pivotal role in meeting global protein demand emphasizes the need for chicken health assurance. This study introduces real-time acoustic monitoring for poultry farms, bridging the gap left by labor-intensive, delayed health issue detection that undermines welfare and profits. We devised a system to capture and analyze farm audio data by harnessing audio analytics and machine learning. Targeted microphones strategically captured chicken vocalizations, with collected audio undergoing preprocessing for Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). Utilizing a comprehensively trained Support Vector Machine (SVM) model, our solution achieved a remarkable accuracy of 95.66% in real-time detection of abnormal sounds. Rigorous experimentation showcased SVM's proficiency in distinguishing between normal and abnormal, further classifying the chicken's activities, and updating the user every 30 minutes. Farmers can intervene on time, ensuring the well-being of their flock. This real-time insight empowers farmers to take immediate corrective actions, enhancing animal welfare, minimizing losses, and optimizing overall farm management practices.

articleTitle: A Novel Scheme Based on Optimization for Controlling the Speed of PMBLDC Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This study employs an innovative PID controller based on optimization to regulate the speed of a Permanent Magnet Brushless DC (PMBLDC) motor. Utilizing Energy Valley Optimizer (EVO), the PID controller is optimized. Popular motor types include PMBLDC motors, which are inexpensive and simple to assemble. The PID controller's high usability is attributable to its straightforward construction and reliable operation. However, tuning the PID controller's parameters is time-consuming, and sometimes, optimal value finding becomes more challenging. So, an error remains between the setpoint and the obtained output signal. The motor's speed is regulated by utilising a novel controller, the EVO-PID controller. The results from the suggested controller are compared to other reported controllers. It is seen from the simulations that the new controller performs better than other controllers.

articleTitle: Motor Bearing Fault Classification using Laser Sensor and Light Weight CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Among the several faults, bearing fault is considered one of the most common and major problems in the motor. In this paper, we present end-to-end motor bearing fault detection and classification employing laser, wavelet transformation and light weight convolution neural network (CNN). The proposed method has three stages: first, raw vibration signatures from the motor shaft vibration operating with healthy and faulty bearing is captured using laser in point and measure fashion. Thereafter, these time domain signals are converted to time-frequency plane using wavelet transform. Finally, the features are extracted from that plane and used to train a light weight CNN model to detect and classify the bearing fault. Experimental findings demonstrates that the laser based method in tandem with CNN model can classify the bearing fault with 99 % accuracy. Further, the proposed model gives similar performance compared with standard models - SqueezeNet, and MobilNet with added benefits of much smaller model parameters and model size which enables efficient deployment on the edge.

articleTitle: Detection of Adulteration in Honey Using a Precision Analog Microcontroller Based System with an Electrochemical Sensor Interface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Honey adulteration is a growing concern in the Indian food industry. In this work, a portable low cost versatile system based on the ADuCM355 microcontroller with an electrochemical interface was designed to detect adulteration in honey. The sensitivity of the technique is demonstrated using jaggery as the prototypical adulterant. The measurement system is capable of measuring the impedance of liquid samples with an accuracy of 1Ω in the frequency range of 1 Hz to 80 KHz. Electrical parameters are extracted by fitting the measured electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) plots to appropriate equivalent circuit models at various concentrations of adulterant. The specific parameters extracted showed deterministic trends as the concentration of adulteration is varied. Linear regression shows promising results for accurately estimating changes in each parameter with the concentration of the adulterant.

articleTitle: Effect of the Dual Attention Suppression Attack on the Performance of Self-Driving Car Models - A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Compared to human-driven cars, full self-driving cars (SDCs) offer greater safety and convenience. However, the liability shifts from the human driver to the car manufacturer, who has to ensure that the SDCs are robust in withstanding any security attack. The Dual Attention Suppression (DAS) attack is a recent visual adversarial attack proposed in the literature that may significantly degrade the performance of an SDC. In this preliminary work, we simulate the DAS attack on SDCs in the CARLA self-driving simulator framework and study the attack's effect on SDC performance. The SDC performance is measured in terms of success rate and driving score. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to perform such a study. We apply a visual static patch at a fixed location on the backside of an ambulance vehicle type to induce the DAS attack. The DAS attack reduces the attention of the “car” class from deep learning models for object classification and object detection. We perform several SDC simulations wherein ambulances with and without modification are spawned randomly as neighboring traffic. Experimental results demonstrate that SDC performance (success rate and driving score) is largely unaffected by the DAS attack. While this initial result is promising, further study with different vehicle types and dynamic visual patch locations is required to generalize the result.

articleTitle: Fortified-Grid 3.0: Security by Design for Smart Grid through Hardware Security Primitives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Traditional approaches to adding security measures and retrofitting them onto existing smart grid systems, have security flaw and vulnerability. Considering security from the beginning, potential vulnerabilities and risks can be identified and addressed early in the smart grid design process, leading to more robust and secure solutions. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>bD involves incorporating security considerations and features into the design and architecture of a system rather than adding them as an afterthought. This paper provides an extensive overview of hardware security and trust, examining threats, countermeasures, and design tools. Fortified-Grid 3.0 introduces the latest advancements in hardware security research, aiming to inspire hardware designers and smart grid developers to embrace the challenges and opportunities of integrating additional security measures into robust hardware design, testing, and verification. This paper also discusses security by design in smart grids, focusing on primitives like PUF and TPM. Our paper addresses various challenges, presents solutions, and conducts comparative analyses of prevalent Security-by-Design approaches.

articleTitle: Power Budget Improvement Using Floorplan Methodologies In Lower(28nm) Technology Node
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The demand for numerous technological devices is rising quickly today. These devices ought to be as small, power-efficient, and effective as possible. The electronics industry has undergone a revolution thanks to integrated circuit technology. To meet demand, the ASIC industry, a significant contributor to electronic systems, is shifting to lower technological nodes. The art of any physical design is in the floorplan. A well- thought-out floor plan results in an ASIC design with increased performance and the ideal amount of space. Floor layout can be difficult because it involves deciding where to put I/O pads, macros, power, and ground structure. To reduce congestion, use floor plan strategies. The floor plan must be improved if traffic congestion is to be reduced. Methods and strategies for reducing congestion are a very noticeable step in the floorplan. The three floor plan implementation methods are demonstrated in this paper, which are data flow analysis (DFA), pin placement, and hierarchical. Using Industry Standard Tool at the 28nm technology node, each methodology's IR drop was calculated and compared with different floorplan methodologies like DFA, pin placement, and hierarchy. According to this work, pin placement is 52% more effective than hierarchical and 73% more efficient than DFA.

articleTitle: CRNN-based UAV Detection using Acoustic Signature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), commonly referred to as drones, have gained significant popularity across various domains. However, their widespread adoption has brought about security concerns in both civilian and military contexts. Real-time detection and identification of UAVs are critical to ensuring safety and security. In this research paper, we propose an innovative method for UAV detection utilizing Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks (CRNNs) based on their distinctive acoustic signatures. We assess the viability and effectiveness of this approach through extensive experimentation and evaluation using a diverse dataset. In our experiments, the acoustic signals emitted by a small UAV (MAVIC 3 Classic) demonstrated an exceptional UAV detection rate of 99.30%, accompanied by an impressively low false detection rate of only 0.69%. It is important to note that the detection range is constrained to approximately 70 meters. This limitation can be attributed to the characteristics of the UAV used in the experiments, which has a weight of approximately 890 grams and employs low-noise propellers, further constraining the detection range. These results underscore the considerable potential of CRNNs in UAV detection, offering a promising solution for addressing UAV-related security threats.

articleTitle: Improved Target Tracking and Fusion Using Optimally Quantized Measurement Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Nowadays, autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) technologies provide localization of AUV s, high-precision 3D measurement mapping, and underwater target tracking. Usually, the AUV consists of various sensors to acquire the dense measurements of the underwater scene to perform target tracking and functionalities. In in-water mobility, the bandwidth is a significant bottleneck, allowing communication with other AUV s and performing centralized target tracking and fusion. Since the communication modules within the AUV are compact, low power, and have low bandwidth, the quantized measurements are transmitted to the fusion center (FC). The sensing devices provide different measurements like range, range rate, azimuth, elevation, and directional cosines corresponding to the scene. Whereas the range measurements are in meters, azimuth measurements range from 0 to 360°• Hence, using a single quantizer with a predefined step size leads to tremendous errors. This paper proposes to deploy an optimal quantizer for every measurement channel and then transmit it to the FC. To explicitly study the quantization effect, we have used linear and optimal quantization techniques which can adaptively choose the levels of the measurements. The extended Kalman filter (EKF) in combination with correlation-free covariance intersection (CI) fusion algorithm is used to attain the global track information. The performance of the proposed method is quantified using the position root mean square error (PRMSE) and compared with the no-quantization state-of-art.

articleTitle: Power Efficient Approximate Ternary Subtractor for Image Processing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The ternary logic has been the most popular in recent years. Many ternary logic-based arithmetic circuits, such as adders and multipliers, exist. Applications such as image processing and video processing application, accurate computation is not necessary, approximate computing is employed to significantly improve circuit parameters such as area, power, and power-delay product. This paper presents a design of an efficient 1-bit approximate half subtractor using the k-map-based methodology, which is used to implement a full subtractor and an 8-bit ternary subtractor. In this work, an error is introduced in the difference signal of the half subtractor. The proposed approximate ternary half subtractor show that power and delay are reduced by 42 % and 55 % in comparison with subtractor using 3: 1 multiplexers and are reduced by 37 % and 38% in contrast with subtractor using 2:1 multiplexer. Finally, the proposed 8-bit subtractor is evaluated using an image processing application.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Cryptographic Acceleration using Hardware-Software Co-Design with RISC-V
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Recent growth in the Internet of Things (IoT) has not only enabled novel applications but also led to new security concerns. Majority of IoT devices are resource-constrained em-bedded systems which make it prohibitively difficult to implement computationally complex cryptographic algorithms and security protocols in software. We demonstrate energy-efficient hardware accelerators for elliptic curve cryptography, lattice-based cryp-tography and pairing-based cryptography integrated with open-source RISC-V micro-processor to achieve up to two orders of magnitude improvement in energy-efficiency and performance through hardware-software co-design.

articleTitle: Smart Non-Invasive Real-Time Health Monitoring using Machine Learning and IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The paper explores a novel approach to health care using Machine Learning and the Internet of Things (IoT) to create a non-invasive real-time health monitoring system. The system uses IoT devices like wearable sensors, smart medical devices, and mobile applications to collect health-related data, including vital signs, activity levels, sleep patterns, and environmental factors. This data is integrated into a centralized cloud-based platform for accessibility and security. Machine Learning algorithms are used to process and interpret the data, detecting anomalies and predicting potential health issues. This allows for personalized health insights and early intervention in preventive healthcare. The system supports user-friendly interfaces, allowing individuals to actively engage in their own health management. Patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals can access intuitive dashboards and receive notifications or alerts when abnormalities are detected, promoting informed decision-making and timely medical interventions. The Smart Non-Invasive Real-Time Health Monitoring system has the potential to transform the healthcare industry by changing the emphasis from responding to illnesses after they occur to actively preventing them beforehand.

articleTitle: loT-based Smart Dustbin for Effective Waste Management
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The numerous urban regions that are now being constructed around the world are causing the area's population density to increase. As a result, there is a higher possibility of an unhealthy atmosphere as waste and trash production rises. In today's culture, especially in India, the majority of people lack a sense of responsibility, and many of us loiter about the rubbish in our surroundings. This project was developed to deal with concerns of this nature, with an emphasis on the cleanliness and hygienic conditions of every given neighborhood. People or any other individual will be compensated for disposing of rubbish or any other kind of waste in the trash can. In addition to materials that deteriorate but do not dissolve, a dustbin is a receptacle used to hold recyclable and non-recyclable rubbish. They are often used in homes, workplaces, and other locations, but when they are full, no one is there to clean them up, causing the waste to pour out. The area around a trash can might enhance pollutants as well. Dustbin air pollution may lead to the growth of bacteria and viruses that can give humans terrible diseases. For trash management, Smart Dustbins are increasingly crucial in the workplace. This study proposes a smart trash can for smart waste management and a sanitary environment. The microcontroller NodeMCU ESP8266 is used to create the system. The moment someone approaches the trash can, it will open on its own. The trashcan will measure the amount of waste, the amount of moisture, and the weight of the waste within the dustbin. All of these measurements will be shown on mobile applications and the computer online. Email management and app notifications will be used to provide notifications of the entire display to computers and mobile devices.

articleTitle: A High Gain Narrow Band CMOS LNA suitable for L1 and L5 band of Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper focuses on the development and testing of a single-stage Low Noise Amplifier(LNA) for wireless applications in the CMOS RF receiver front end. The proposed LNA achieves higher gain and lower noise figure values which are obtained at 1.176GHz and 1.575GHz frequencies with 1.5V and 1.8V supply voltages. The single-stage cascode LNA has been designed using UMC 180nm technology in cadence virtuoso for L-band. The L-band is used by satellites in low-Earth orbit. The L-band radio frequency is suited for most LEO platform applications, such as marine and long-distance aircraft communications.

Author Keywords: Narrow Band(NB) CS LNA with Inductive source degeneration

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of Decimal to BCD Encoder using Modified-GDI Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The main constraints in recent trends of VLSI technology are low power and small area. This paper presents the implementation of Decimal to BCD encoder using Modified Gate Diffusion Input technique. Compared with CMOS and Gate Diffusion Input technique-based Decimal to BCD encoder in terms of power consumption, surface area, transistor counts and Propagation Delay. This encoder is implemented using NG-Spice on 180nm technology.

articleTitle: Design of Low Noise, High Sensitive Front End Electronics for the Charge Readout from Silicon Photomultiplier Detector foR Future Space Exploration Programs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The detection of low energy X-rays in the space exploration programs is a key to determine various scientific information for e.g. mapping of elemental composition of the planetary bodies. Scintillation detector along with the Silicon Photomultiplier (SiPM) is used for the development of the circuits for the detection of low energy X-rays. The design of the circuits is carried out keeping in mind the range of output charge of the SiPM. The circuits have been designed, simulated and realized in the lab which detects < 0.5 Pico Coulomb (pC) charge. The circuits presented here are charge sensitive preamplifier (CSPA) using RC feedback technique, and Gaussian shaping amplifier consisting of high pass and low pass filters to improve the signal to noise ratio. In the test results, 59.54 keV energy from 241Am radioactive source is measured with 10 keV lower energy threshold.

articleTitle: P-ReTiNA: Photonic Tensor Core Based Real- Time AI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Computing deep AI algorithms on traditional CPUs and GPUs brings several performance and energy pitfalls. Several novel approaches based on ASIC, FPGA, and resistive-memory devices have been recently demonstrated with promising results. Most of them target only the inference (testing) phase of deep learning. There have been very limited attempts to design a full-fledged AI accelerator capable of both training and inference in realtime. It is due to the highly compute and memory intensive nature of the training phase. In this paper, we propose P- ReTiNA, a novel analog photonics CNN accelerator. P- ReTinA uses silicon microdisk-based convolution, photonic phase change memory-based memory, and dense- wavelength-division-multiplexing for energy-efficient and ultrafast deep learning. We evaluate P-ReTinA using a commercial CAD framework (IPKISS) on deep learning benchmark models including LeNet and VGG-Net. Compared to the state-of-the-art, P-ReTinA improves the CNN throughput, energy-efficiency, and computational efficiency by up to 48<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>, 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>, and 12x respectively with trivial accuracy degradation.

articleTitle: QPUF: Quantum Physical Unclonable Functions for Security-by-Design of Industrial Internet-of-Things
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This work presents a Quantum Computing based Physical Unclonable Functions (PUF) architecture with a novel approach for PUF key generation and noise reduction in noisy Quantum systems. The motivation is to explore the potential of Quantum Computing assisted cybersecurity for Security-by-Design (SbD) of Industrial-Internet-of-Things (IIoT). Internet-of-Things (IoT) in Industry 4.0 can improve efficiency, increase automation, and facilitate intelligent decision making through the integration of edge cloud computing paradigms. However, the lack of standardization of security protocols across IIoT devices can be challenging due to the heterogeneous nature of these devices. In this context, a novel Quantum circuits based PUF design that is built on real Quantum hardware is presented. The proposed QPUF can facilitate security in IIoT by using a Quantum hardware generated PUF key as the device identity. The proposed PUF Design is built using Quantum Hadamard Gate, and Ry gates and has been experimentally demonstrated on IBM Quantum hardware systems. The proposed architecture also supports PUF key generation from Quantum hardware for security applications. Figures-of-merits (FoM) of PUF have been evaluated and presented to demonstrate the robustness of the proposed Quantum PUF for SbD of IIoT.

articleTitle: Analysis of PDMS Polymeric Material for Heavy Metal Ions Sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Recently, the polymer materials like polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) emerges as the new class of materials for microelectromechanical (MEMS) devices. The MEMS fabricated with these materials can be used in biosensing applications since these materials has high sensitivity and excellent bending properties. In the present study, the physical parameters of the microcantilevers were analyzed and optimized with the COMSOL Multiphysics software to explore its application in the MEMS Biosensing field. The design in this work offers a stiffness of 0.196 N/m, sensitivity of 0.32064 mΩ/ Ω/Pa, change in resistance of 8.016 mΩ with the applied force of 500-1000nN and the resonating frequency supported by the design is 4.8 kHz. The proposed design after fabrication will be proved to be a cost-effective design having simplified process design steps in comparison to the silicon micro fabrication which is costly and requires complex process flow.

articleTitle: IoT and ML based Smart Pill Dispenser (SPD) Application for Monitoring Elderly People
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: With the increase in health issues these days, a majority of the people are adhered to medication. There might be a chance that most of them may forget to take their medications as prescribed due to a variety of factors such as busy schedule, mental stress, health issues, and so on. As a result, it may take longer to recover from illness and origin for side effects as well, especially for elderly. Henceforth, it is necessary that the patient must take the relevant medications in the correct dosage and at the correct time. In this paper, an approach has been proposed using internet of things (loT) that guides the elderly people to take the proper medication on time. The proposed smart pill Dispenser (SPD) system is economical and effective. Also, a web application is integrated that collects the information about the diabetes and heart disease of each patient. Further, machine learning models are embedded in order to predict the chance of diabetes, heart stroke, and kidney disease for the patient. This would be economical and effective model to dispense the medicines on time to the elderly people.

articleTitle: Integrated IoT-Based Air Quality Monitoring and Prediction System: A Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Air pollution remains a global concern, leading to approximately 7 million annual deaths from prolonged exposure to harmful pollutants, causing chronic illnesses like respiratory diseases, cardiovascular problems, and cancer. It also has adverse effects on ecosystems due to climate changes. Governments rely on air quality monitoring systems to regulate toxic gas emissions, safeguarding public health and supporting agriculture and industry. Recent years have seen increased interest in air quality measurement and prediction. By connecting sensors in different locations, It is simpler to detect air pollution thanks to the Internet of Things (IoT). In order to conduct a full analysis, our research simulates air quality patterns in specific regions using an assortment of stationary and portable IoT sensors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method for detecting and forecasting air quality, offering efficient monitoring, particularly for smart cities and businesses, using machine learning algorithms and data from the real world.

articleTitle: Improved Human Activity Recognition Technique with Multi-Class Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Recognition of human activity is a current, difficult, and demanding area of research that seeks to comprehend human behavior by evaluating sensory data gathered from people and their surroundings. Here, a system called Human Activity Recognition (HAR) is proposed to comprehend human behavior through the interpretation of sensory data using Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN). WBAN offers long-term continuous tracking over or inside the body of a person and may facilitate the transmission of real-time traffic as data, voice, and video. To deal with this problem, our approach employs a multi-class Support Vector Machine (SVM) for determining the probability of each action. With the objective to develop an appropriate HAR methodology, the purpose of this article is to resolve the HAR problem in wireless body area networks.

articleTitle: Design, Development and Testing of Electronic Control Unit Prototype in an Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: An Electronic Control Unit (ECU) acts as a vehicle's the central hub, managing functions through microcontrollers that interpret sensor input and ensure smooth operation. Over 50 microcontrollers govern the operation of low-voltage components like indicators, horns, regenerative brakes, air conditioners, power windows and airbag deployment to monitor control, and enhance diverse aspects, such as engine and motor modules' suspension, powertrain, transmission, brakes, and body functions. This paper delves into the hardware design of an electric vehicle powered by a 48V Lithium Nickel Manganese Cobalt Oxide (Li-NMC) battery. To efficiently utilize this voltage, a buck converter steps it down to 12V for the low-voltage system, with voltage regulators further reducing it to 5V for the microcontroller board's operation. Inputs from buttons like start, brake, charge, accelerator, forward, and reverse are processed by the microcontroller board and Motor Controller. They, in turn, control various LED pins to indicate different states of the car system. The system, designed for an all-terrain vehicle, underwent rigorous testing with a Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motor, achieving 45 km/hr and 5.16 m/s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> acceleration. The implementation uses an Arduino board and C language to enhance the vehicle functionality by enabling user interactions, such as starting the car, applying brakes, charging, and controlling acceleration, all while providing clear visual feedback through LED indicators. This paper exemplifies the potential of readily available microcontroller applications for EVs and provides a forward looking vision for an all-terrain four-wheel electric vehicle, showcasing the energy-efficient utilization of low-voltage systems through readily available electronic circuit boards.

articleTitle: Low Power and Area-Efficient Hybrid Adder for ALU Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This study describes a new low-power, area-efficient hybrid adder architecture for arithmetic logic unit (ALU) operations in digital systems. The goal is to integrate multiple adder architectures to reduce power consumption while increasing speed. The proposed hybrid adder combines pass transistor logic (PTL), gate diffusion input (GDI) logic, and modified GDI (MGDI) logic to provide carry and sum outputs, that reduces power consumption and improve circuit performance, with less number of transistor count. Cadence Virtuoso is used for evaluation using a 45 nm generic process design kit (GPDK) and the power supply voltage is set at 1.2 V. A comparative analysis with the existing adders has been performed considering parameters like propagation delay (PD), average power (AP), and power delay product (PDP). By balancing power consumption, circuit performance, and space utilization, the research adds to adder design. Designers and researchers of efficient adders in portable and battery-powered devices will find this information useful.

articleTitle: Overview of Cryo-CMOS Devices and Circuits for Quantum Computing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: A fault tolerant scalable quantum computer requires more than 1000 Qubits to perform real time state correction and to improve the Qubit coherence time. The dense wiring connections required between the quantum processor placed at a 100 mK temperature and the room temperature control and readout electronics serve as a limiting factor in this system. Qubit control and readout electronics operating at 4 K temperature, placed closer to a quantum processor inside the dilution refrigerator avoids the dense wiring connections to room temperature electronics, and hence, serve as a potential solution to realize a scalable quantum computer. However, with no CMOS process technology models available at cryogenic temperatures, the design of a fully integrated, ultra-low power Qubit control and readout electronics at a sub-1 mW power consumption proves to be extremely challenging. In recent years, there has been a huge rise in interest among the research communities to understand and solve the device and circuit level challenges at deep cryogenic temperatures. This paper presents an overview of the recently published active and passive device nonidealities, circuit design challenges and solutions, and the future research directions in the Qubit control and readout electronics operating at deep cryogenic temperatures.

articleTitle: Designing Optimized and Secured Reusable Convolutional Hardware Accelerator Against IP Piracy Using Retina Biometrics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel secure high-level synthesis (HLS) methodology for designing an optimized and secure reusable convolutional hardware accelerator against intellectual property (IP) piracy using retinal signature. These reusable hardware accelerator designs used in system-on-chips (SoCs) of computing systems are susceptible to the hardware threat of piracy. Therefore, the proposed approach firstly performs compiler driven high level transformation in order to optimize the design latency, followed by embedding the retinal biometric signature of IP vendor in the form of encoded hardware security constraints into structurally transformed scheduled design during register allocation module of HLS. These embedded security constraints thereby enable the robust detection against pirated design versions. The proposed approach achieves the following: i) optimized and secure design for convolutional hardware accelerator ii) robust detection against piracy at zero design cost overhead iii) significantly lower probability of coincidence (Px) indicating stronger digital evidence and higher tamper tolerance (TT) than recent approaches.

articleTitle: Design of Low Power ALU for RISC-VISA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: RISC-V, an open and versatile Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), offers numerous enhancements and serves as a flexible foundation for incorporating optional additions that facilitate the development of general-purpose software. Processor designers primarily aim to enhance power efficiency and reduce latency in their designs. Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU) unit being the element of the processor consuming more computational power becomes the target of our work. In our design, we adopted the open-source RISC-VISA standard and redesigned the ALU unit of the processor for better power efficiency. In this research, we have successfully implemented a unique latch-based ALU architecture that demonstrates improved resource utilization. By strategically incorporating latches, we have effectively enabled the computational blocks specific to the desired operation, resulting in enhanced efficiency. The entire design is implemented using traditional Verilog. The design has been synthesized in the Cadence Genus synthesis platform using 90nm technology. Our work has shown a significant reduction of 9.44 % in the total power consumption.

articleTitle: Domino Logic based Noise Immune Schmitt Trigger Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper highlights noise-immune Schmitt trigger circuits with improved hysteresis width. Dual Purpose Schmitt Trigger (DPST) is employed as a dual purpose owing to the addition of a control module and can act as a domino logic as well as a Schmitt trigger (ST) circuit. Major performance parameters such as hysteresis width, power consumption, delay, and process variation of HW are calculated for different ST circuits. All simulation work has been carried out using the UMC 40nm CMOS technology with Cadence virtuoso tool. The proposed ST has 1.23×, 3.77×, and 1.17× less dynamic power dissipation, leakage power dissipation, and delay, respectively, as compared to conventional ST which makes it a more efficient ST. The hysteresis width of the proposed ST is 1.11× more than the conventional circuit. The higher hysteresis width than that of other reported circuits makes it more practical for use in a noisy environment.

articleTitle: Optimization of Imprecise Multiplier Circuits by using Binary Decision Diagram
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Imprecise multipliers are employed to enhance the efficiency and reduce the power consumption of arithmetic circuits while tolerating acceptable levels of inaccuracy in the outcomes. The multiplier circuit has a broader range of applications within embedded systems, particularly in the fields of digital signal processing, IoT and multimedia, etc. We proposed a systematic formal approach utilizing the Look-Up Table (LUT) employing the Burch method to evaluate the imprecise multiplier based on the Binary Decision Diagram (BDD) considering Worst Case Error constraint. Implemented 13 bit multiplier using normal and proposed imprecise multiplier shows 98% reduction in number of nodes. The proposed 25 bit imprecise multiplier based on Burch HL shows an 89% decrement in a number of nodes w.r.t. Burch LH method. BDD generation for imprecise multiplier is 75% faster than normal.

articleTitle: FruitPAL: A Smart Healthcare Framework for Automatic Detection of Fruit Allergens
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: To maintain good health, people should take care of their dietary choices to boost their immune system. Immune disorders, such as Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) and fruit allergy, can compromise the immune system. Fruit allergy is a prevalent medical condition that impacts the immune system due to the nutritional significance of fruit as a food source. Individuals with fruit allergy who exhibit a deficiency in recognizing the possible risks of consuming fruits should be subjected to close monitoring. This paper proposes a device called “FruitPAL’ designed to precisely recognize allergenic fruits and alert the caregiver to take necessary precautions for people with fruit allergies. FruitPAL can predict what fruit causes allergies in real-time to protect the immune system from any harm. YOLOv8, the most recent iteration of the YOLO series, has been incorporated into FruitPAL to increase precision and decrease time response. Using the technology of YOLOv8 in the FruitPAL device enhances the protection of people allergic to fruit.

articleTitle: Real-Time Castor Leaf Disease Detection Using Machine Learning on Edge AI Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Castor leaf diseases can have a significant impact on farmers in India, as agriculture is a major sector of the Indian economy, and many farmers rely on their crops for their livelihoods. Diseases can cause significant damage to crop, leading to lower yields and poor-quality produce. This can result in reduced income for farmers and, in severe cases, may even lead to crop failure and financial losses. This paper proposes a deep learning-based castor leaf disease detection system that discriminates the castor disease into three different types that are Leaf spot, Wilt, and Alternaria blight. The dataset is manually collected using drones as well as other sources and is annotated and labeled for training the machine learning models. Various versions of You Only Look Once (YOLO) object detection algorithms are employed for the training and detection of the disease on castor leaves in this work. The performance of these models is compared for real-time inference as well as tested on actual leaves in a castor farm. From the experimental results, it is concluded that YOLOv8 gives a higher outcome than the other versions of the YOLO model in terms of mean average precision, Precision and Recall. The proposed model is deployed on the Xilinx Kria KV 260 FPGA for real-time inference.

articleTitle: IR Drop Mitigation Methodologies in 90nm Technology Node for Networking Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The IR Drop effect in lower technology nodes(<90nm) technologies and associated mitigation strategies are presented in depth in this research. Due to lower technology nodes and resistance, resulting in high voltage drop in the design. Hence network chip and high-end applications, SoC design so significant for IR drop. With the scalability of the technology, the IR Drop in the power planning rises at a fast rate. It was demonstrated that in modern and complex designs using Concrete methodologies like wire sizing and the insertion of decoupling capacitors, prevents IR drop. This paper presented adaptive metal width variation to improve the IR drop. In 90nm technology node, 12% improvement in IR drop found with 76% variation in the stripes metal width.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Modified Lightweight 128-Bit AES Algorithm for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The rapidly increasing use of IoT devices necessitates a suitable encryption algorithm for data security. The widely used Advanced Encryption Standard algorithm (AES) algorithm is computationally complex, thus unsuitable for resource-constrained IoT devices. The proposed work implements optimized alternatives for the 128-bit AES algorithm stages, aiming to minimize power and memory usage. A Modified Lightweight variant of AES was developed using Verilog HDL and implemented on Artix-7 Basys-3 FPGA board. It was found that the total on-chip power required by the modified variant has been reduced by 81.92 % for encryption and 47.21 % for decryption. There is a significant decrease in the number of LUTs required with 76.84% for encryption and 53.53% for decryption, making it a suitable algorithm for IoT lightweight applications.

articleTitle: Metaheuristic Approach for Bearing Fault Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper presents a study on ball-bearing fault prediction using a combination of Genetic Algorithm and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithms. The selection of features used to develop machine learning plays an important role in building models. Ant Colony Optimization Technique is used for feature selection, Genetic Algorithm for hyper-parameter selection, and comparison of accuracies among different classifiers to choose the best model among others. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving fault prediction accuracy. Random Forest Classifier with Ant Colony Optimization gives an accuracy of nearly 95%.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Computation in Constrained Systems with Machine Learning Workloads
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Increasing demand for energy-efficient systems with machine learning workloads requires the exploration of various avenues for lowering consumption in energy-constrained edge devices. Memories, specifically Static Random Access Memories (SRAMs), are essential to today's system-on-chips (SoCs). In-memory computation (IMC) enables significant improvements in efficiency by combining data storage with computation. An SRAM macro was introduced to support continuous-sensing applications via simultaneous data buffering, always-on energy/area-efficient computing for continuous event detection, as well as reduced bitline activity without the need for any data prediction for energy-efficient bulk read. Secure integrated systems routinely require the generation of keys in the form of dynamic entropy from True Random Number Generators (TRNGs), and static entropy from Physically Unclonable Functions (PUFs). We introduced an SRAM with a unified TRNG and multi-bit PUF for complete in-memory dynamic and static entropy generation for low-cost security, both in terms of area and design. Applications such as sensor-rich robotics, smart surfaces, and prosthetics demand electronic skin solutions with human-like tactile receptor density. Such densities are supported using a tactile sensing system with area and energy/receptor suitable for aggregation of thousands of receptors while keeping sub-0.01mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/receptor area efficiency and chip power to the mW range for straightforward power distribution over stretchable substrates with tens of cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>area and long-lived untethered operation, requiring sub-uW/receptor power.

articleTitle: Enhanced Smart Stick Design for Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: In a world propelled by technological advancements, there exists a pressing need to address the challenges faced by individuals with impaired mobility. The Smart Stick integrates advanced components such as an ESP-32 microcontroller, A9 GSM/GPRS module, ultrasonic and water sensors, along with a speaker and microphone, with a primary focus on providing a versatile and comprehensive aid for users. Emphasizing user-friendliness and lightweight design, the Smart Stick incorporates voice assistance technology to offer real-time guidance, ensuring a seamless experience for users with diverse needs. It's ability to detect obstacles and identify potential hazards through ultrasonic and water sensors significantly contributes to the safety and confidence of individuals navigating their surroundings. Further-more, the feature of live location tracking and emergency calling capabilities through the A9 GSM/GPRS module extends its utility beyond daily navigation, providing an added layer of security and peace of mind for both users and their caregivers. This Smart Stick project not only marks a significant stride in the evolution of assistive technology but also presents a versatile and adaptable solution that embraces the latest technological advancements to empower individuals with enhanced mobility, independence, and safety.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of PRNU-Based Forensic Techniques in Mobile Devices using Peak Correlation Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: In the digital age, this pioneering investigation is the initial endeavor to confront a crucial challenge in image forensics, marking a notable advancement. The implementation of photoresponse non-uniformity (PRNU) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in their respective applications, leading to a noteworthy enhancement in forensic techniques for image analysis. The increasing difficulty of manipulating images underscores the need for forensic methods that are both accurate and efficient. This research specifically delves into the combined use of photo-response non-uniformity (PRNU) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to boost the efficiency of picture forensics. The methodology involves PRNU analyzing visual noise patterns and comparing them with CNN's expertise in eliminating distinguishing elements to determine the source of an image. Results from the experiments highlight that the integration of PRNU and CNNs achieves an exceptional level of efficiency, evident in a peak correlation coefficient (PCC) value of 0.989 and an accuracy rate of 89.47 percent on the CIFAR-10 dataset. This integrated approach proves beneficial across various forensic applications, including forgery detection, identification of image modifications, and tracking manipulated images. However, limitations arise due to the inherent characteristics of the gadget used in the study. Ongoing research efforts are directed towards establishing more advanced models, incorporating additional forensic techniques, and developing machine learning algorithms. This ongoing work aims to address these limitations and significantly enhance the precision of photo-matching in image forensics.

articleTitle: Area-Efficient In-Memory Computation with Improved Linearity using Voltage-Controlled Delay Cell-based Ring Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: The hardware accelerators are essential for high-performance and energy-efficient implementation of machine learning algorithms in hardware. The multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operation is the fundamental operation in the machine learning algorithm. In this work, we proposed an in-memory computation architecture using a 6T SRAM array along with a specialized delay cell in which the multiplication operation of the MAC is performed in the voltage domain, and the accumulation operation of the MAC is performed in the time domain. The proposed delay cells can be cascaded to form a ring oscillator (RO), which converts the value of the MAC to the frequency of the RO. A simple digital counter is sufficient to measure the frequency of the RO. The counter occupies less area than the analog-to-digital converter (ADC), needed for voltage-domain-based IMC, and the time-to-digital converter (TDC), needed for time-domain-based IMC. The simulation of the proposed architecture in an industrial 65 nm process achieves 10.32/1321.2 GOPS, 30.3149.5 TOPSIW energy for serial/parallel access of rows, and 99% classification accuracy on the MNIST images.

articleTitle: Memristors: Device Modeling, Design and Verification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: In-Memory Computing (IMC) using memristors is considered as one of the most researched topic in recent years. Since the first fabrication of the memristor in 2008, its popularity has expanded to a great extent. Researchers from various diverse domains have explored and contributed to the fabrication and design of the memristor device that in turn aids in the development of crossbar designs for IMC. IMC architectures have the potential to bridge the processor-memory speed gap that exists in current von-Neumann architectures. But due to the variability challenges of the memristive devices being an emerging technology, the technology requires time to mature to be widely adopted by the industry. Research is ongoing and there have been significant efforts from both academia and industry to push this technology forward to the next level. In this paper we aim to provide a brief overview of the various works that have been considered over the last one and a half decade in the broad area of modeling, design, mapping, testing, and verification of the memristor-based circuits and systems.

articleTitle: iTMS:Development of loT based low-cost storage parameters monitoring system for Tomato
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: This paper researches on an Internet of Things (loT) based system developed, using low-cost sensors, which is used for real-time monitoring of respiratory parameters like measuring of temperature, mixed gas concentrations and relative humidity of tomato, stored inside the chamber (acrylic) of 1 cubic foot, under the ambient conditions. In this system, real time data can be viewed also on personal computer and cloud server.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach using ARIMA, Kalman Filter and LSTM for Accurate Wind Speed Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Present energy demand and modernization are leading to greater fossil fuel consumption, which has increased environmental pollution and led to climate change. Hence to decrease dependency on conventional energy sources, renewable energy sources are considered. Wind energy is a long-term renewable energy resource but its intermittent nature makes it difficult in harnessing it Since wind speed prediction is vital there are different methodologies for wind speed estimation available in the literature. In this work, a new hybrid model is proposed by combining auto-regressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), Kalman filter and long short-term memory (LSTM) for estimating wind speed which works more accurately than the existing methods proposed in the literature. From simulations, it is observed that the proposed method works with better accuracy when compared to the existing methods.

articleTitle: Detecting Forged Facial Videos Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: In this paper, we propose to detect forged videos, of faces, in online videos. To facilitate this detection, we propose to use smaller (fewer parameters to learn) convolutional neural networks (CNN), for a data-driven approach to forged video detection. To validate our approach, we investigate the Face-Forensics public dataset detailing both frame-based and video-based results. The proposed method is shown to outperform current state of the art. We also perform an ablation study, analyzing the impact of batch size, number of filters, and number of network layers on the accuracy of detecting forged videos.

articleTitle: Key-Driven Multi-Layered Structural Obfuscation of IP cores using Reconfigurable Obfuscator based Network Challenge and Switch Control Logic
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: A novel key-driven multi-layered structural obfuscation of IP cores using a reconfigurable obfuscator based on network challenge and switch control logic is presented in this paper. The proposed methodology incorporates a robust reconfigurable obfuscator unit comprising of scalable gate architecture network topologies driven through challenge and switch control bits capable of generating multiple structurally obfuscated IP core designs with equivalent functionality useful for consumer electronics (CE) systems. The proposed approach is capable of producing multi-layered structurally obfuscated designs through a series of robust key-driven transformations for securing against reverse engineering. Results suggest that the proposed approach yields significantly enhanced encoded key strength used for obfuscation, requires significantly greater attackers' effort in deobfuscation of the original design and higher strength of obfuscation in terms of modified gates, compared to a recent approach.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of “ARP Block” using 28nm Technology node
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: ASICs, or Application Specific Integrated Circuits, are integrated circuits that have been built for a specific usage or application, as the name implies. By decreasing the size of electrical goods and increasing the density of logic gates per chip, ASIC contributed to transform technology. Moore's law states that technology is progressing at a breakneck pace. With the progress of cutting-edge technologies into the deep submicron zone, the performance of integrated circuits is being tested by the aggravation of process variability. To meet timing limitations, physical design engineers employ several EDA tools including as ICC, ICC2, Innovus, PrimeTime, Fusion compiler, and others to optimize power, area, timing, and congestion. Timing optimization solutions must be addressed throughout certain stages of Physical design flow. In this paper, back-end design (PnR) is performed on modules called ARP Block using 28nm technology node. The entire chip is divided into clusters, and each cluster is partitioned into several blocks. ARP Block is the name of the block. We will use several timing optimization tactics to try to improve the overall worst negative slack (Setup Violation) of the timing path group REG2REG at floor-plan stage and placement stage (PNR stages) by implementing 28nm technology in the ICC tool. Nevertheless, relative to the literature survey, we decreased the time violation by 43 percent.

articleTitle: W-DaM: Weather Data Management in Smart Agriculture using Blockchain-as-a-Service
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Weather plays a vital role in growing and securing the yield of crops. The data collected from forecasts through different sources have been helpful in avoiding some calamities. The forecast applications are built with conventional database systems; processing and reaching real-time data without being tampered with for farmers is a bottleneck. Most of the time, weather providers' data doesn't match what happens in the farming fields. These differences can lead to heavy damage, especially during unexpected weather strikes. In the current age, smart agriculture makes use of modern equipment such as sensors and satellites that give forecasts more precisely and carefully compiled. The present paper shows an Edge hub near the IoAT device that controls all sensor devices to establish bidirectional communication and embeds Blockchain-as-a-Service (BaaS) for weather data integrity in immediate time. We present a novel architecture with algorithms for this weather data management system and implement the system to see the performance with real-time sensor data.

articleTitle: HIdentifier: A Method in Agriculture CPS Framework to Automatically Identify Disease Hotspots Using Message Passing in Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Smart Electronic Systems (iSES)
abstract: Plant diseases affect the health and yield of the crop which can in turn impact farmers economically and pose a threat to food security across the globe. To protect crops from disease and obtain high yield, many Agriculture Cyber-Physical Systems (A-CPS) have been developed with the ability to detect the presence of a disease. In addition, to effectively control the spread of the disease and reduce its impact on the crops, insights on the spread of the disease and locations of disease hotspots that act as sources for the disease must be identified. HIdentifier proposes a novel graph-based spatial analysis method that takes segmented images of the diseased farmland as input. All the identified disease segments in the input image are represented as a graph to capture the spatial relation between diseased locations.
